title: San Marcos — Citywide Zoning Ban on Data Centers
summary: On June 16, 2026, the San Marcos City Council voted 4–3 to amend its land development code to define data centers and make them ineligible in every zoning district — effectively barring new data center construction anywhere in the city. Reporting describes it as the first outright ban of its kind by a Texas city. It takes the form of a permanent zoning-code change rather than a temporary moratorium.
whyItMatters: The ban is being watched as a test case for how much authority Texas cities retain to block water- and power-hungry data centers. A state senator has signaled a legal challenge, arguing it functions as a de facto moratorium capped by state law; land-use experts counter that a zoning change is not a moratorium.
stageNote: In effect; a state-law challenge has been threatened.
